hypothesis: The frame-path changes in the render worker reduce per-frame CPU work toward the design budgets without raising code size.
prediction: Targets (maxima unless noted) with baselines counted from the integration base for a 1920x1080 profile 4 frame and the 1280x720 display frame. CPU bytes stored by the worker per frame: baseline 60.2 MB at 1080p, 17.4 MB at 720p; target scanout 17 KiB plus 128 marker bytes, read-back adds 8.3 MB poison at 1080p until coverage passes. CPU cache maintenance: baseline 68.5 MB, 21.1 MB; target bytes written plus 256 marker bytes, a read-back frame once. AT translations per frame: about 38,000 plus 8,100 for read-back; target 0. Output check iterations: 2,074,624 guard words plus 2,048 depth guards; target two marker comparisons and two statistics words. Copies per input, displayed and read-back byte: 3 (texture every frame), 3 plus two SHA-256 passes, 3; target 1 per upload, 0, 1. Queue round trips per read-back frame: 254 at 1080p, 114 at 720p; target 2. Worker instructions per 16-batch frame not measured; target 100,000, completion to input return 5,000 with no tick wait and 2 context switches. Worker and client wake-ups beyond interrupts: one per tick of rendering; target 2 each. KCCB kicks and return-slot waits 2 and 2; target 2 and 0. DSB and DMB per frame not measured; target 2 DMB OSHST per kick. IPIs per presented frame target 4; GPU interrupt to RCQ submit target no tick wait, 2 context switches, 1 IPI. Display wakes per second about 1,000, 14 replay register accesses, 1 status read per tick, 22-read scan per replay; target 180, 14 replay, 22-read scan, 2 status reads per boundary. Frame-end to slot return target 1.2 ms; largest render time at 60 Hz with four slots target 15 ms (minimum). GPU leaf PTEs per session excluding the parameter buffer: about 9,000 at 1080p profile 2; targets 6,660 at 1080p read-back and 4,410 at 720p scanout, 4,260 and 2,010 with 64 KiB pages, 4,100 and 1,850 with 2 MiB pages. Parameter buffer: (maximum + 28) x 4 KiB grown inside it; target 16,412 PTEs, 67.2 MB at OPEN, no growth. Indices admitted per frame: 65,535 at every configuration; target the admission formula. Lease bytes excluding the parameter buffer: 36.7 MB at 1080p profile 2 with a 4 MiB display bank; target 29.2 MB at 1080p read-back, 20.0 MB at 720p scanout, 52 KiB bank. Shutdown stop request to PMIC park: GPU closed before TV0 stops; target inside the 2-second HDMI stop reserve.

conclusion: Every measured metric is equal to or better than the base, except the render image bss, which grows by 256 bytes for the batch copy the design requires. Metrics outside their targets each have a closing item (input lending, scanout slots with freshness markers, the coverage board item, the one-reply READ, GPU interrupt delivery, the payload check at OPEN, the multi-range maintenance call, DMB OSHST). The design's AT baseline of about 38,000 plus 8,100 was not reproduced (harness counts 66,457 at 1080p and 24,853 at 720p at the base); the steady-state value of zero meets the target either way.
narrative: Host-model measurement; no board. Wait counts for the base are historical synthetic scheduler counts for the frozen sources; the current texture fixture measures render-service work without simulating scheduler waits (dedicated FreeRTOS worker checks cover timed pacing). hypothesis: Profile 5, scanout slots and the large-page and barrier changes behave as designed on the board.
prediction: Board runs that confirm the design: HDMI capture at 60 Hz of alternating high-contrast frames rendered while the DE scans shows no torn or stale lines and DE underflow status stays clear; retirement isolation (a frame-unique marker written into a returned slot's first and last rows never appears in an earlier captured frame; a second run tests a one-frame-end rule that would allow three slots); large pages one size per run, 64 KiB first (a pattern at a known physical offset renders correctly, canaries outside each page unchanged); parameter buffer (free-list allocated page count at pvr_rogue_fwif.h:2060 read at geometry completion for each scene's largest admitted frame stays inside the bound, both statistics zero; a larger count shrinks the index limits); geometry and fragment time per scene frame from counter samples at the two timeline interrupts; kick ordering (a long run of kicks with DMB OSHST before the doorbell overwrites every marker, no firmware command fault); full tile coverage (no read-back frame contains poison); every completion by interrupt, no surviving marker, no GPU MMU fault, shutdown within the HDMI stop reserve, scenes match the host renderer within the conformance tolerances. Retire-rule reasoning: with one present per 16.667 ms a slot loaded at boundary k returns at boundary k+3 plus the observation delay and is presented again at k+4; the render window is the period minus that delay and the replay burst, giving the 15 ms budget. Parameter-buffer bound: B*T*24 + N*T*8 <= 48 MiB with B = ceil(E*P/128) + N; index limits 65,535 (1x, no clipping), 6,801 (720p 4x with clipping), 12,891 (1080p 1x with clipping).
conclusion: Not yet run; profile 5, scanout slots and freshness markers are not implemented.
narrative: Planned runs, none performed. Design lease-size and PTE targets are in the design doc table and in gpu-graphics-frame-path.
